pr.title: coverage: Add debugging flag `-Zcoverage-options=no-mir-spans`
pr.author: Zalathar

analysis.originalLogic: In `compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/coverage/mappings.rs`, `extract_all_mapping_info_from_mir` had a special case: if `hir_info.is_async_fn`, it skipped all MIR-span extraction and kept only a signature-derived mapping ("An async function desugars into a function that returns a future," "... so just keep the signature span and ignore all of the spans in the MIR body."). For all non-async functions it called `extract_refined_covspans(mir_body, hir_info, basic_coverage_blocks, &mut code_mappings)` to extract coverage spans from MIR statements/terminators, then always extended `branch_pairs` via `extract_branch_pairs(...)` and called `extract_mcdc_mappings(...)`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation for the new `no-mir-spans` debug mode is to treat "skip MIR spans" as "emit no code mappings at all" (or to skip branch/MCDC extraction along with ordinary spans). That is wrong on two source-backed counts: (1) the new `no-mir-spans` branch must reuse the async-function treatment, i.e. "we need to give the same treatment to _all_ functions", which still pushes a mapping when `hir_info.fn_sig_span_extended` is `Some`, because "`llvm-cov` seems to ignore functions that don't have any ordinary code spans"; (2) only `extract_refined_covspans` is gated by the flag, while `branch_pairs.extend(extract_branch_pairs(...))` and `extract_mcdc_mappings(...)` remain unconditional, so branch/condition/MC-DC mappings must still be produced. The corrected transformation is: if `hir_info.is_async_fn || tcx.sess.coverage_no_mir_spans()`, optionally push the signature-span `CodeMapping { span, bcb: START_BCB }`, else call `extract_refined_covspans`; then in both cases continue with branch and MCDC extraction.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust functions instrumented for coverage in MIR, including non-async functions and async functions, with and without `-Zcoverage-options=no-mir-spans`, possibly combined with `branch`, `condition`, or `mcdc` coverage levels. Relevant IR facts are the presence/absence of `hir_info.fn_sig_span_extended`, MIR statements/terminators carrying coverage-eligible spans, and branch/MCDC markers in the body.
analysis.summary: Adds `-Zcoverage-options=no-mir-spans`, an internal debugging option that suppresses ordinary block coverage spans extracted from MIR statements/terminators. It reuses the async-function signature-only treatment for all functions, but must still emit a signature span (otherwise llvm-cov ignores the function) and must still extract branch/MCDC mappings. Regression tests exercise while-loop conditions (plain, negated, `&&`, `||`) and compare `.cov-map`/`.coverage` output.
analysis.trigger: Enabled when the compiler is invoked with `-Zcoverage-options=no-mir-spans` (parsed as `"no-mir-spans" => slot.no_mir_spans = true`), causing `tcx.sess.coverage_no_mir_spans()` to be true during coverage instrumentation of any function. This is documented as: "When set, this flag skips the code that normally extracts coverage spans from MIR statements and terminators. That sometimes makes it easier to debug branch coverage and MC/DC coverage instrumentation, because the coverage output is less noisy."
preconditions: Coverage instrumentation is enabled for the function and `extract_all_mapping_info_from_mir` is reached.
The debugging flag is set via `-Zcoverage-options=no-mir-spans`; it is explicitly 'For internal debugging only.'
If the function has a usable `hir_info.fn_sig_span_extended`, that signature mapping must still be emitted under the flag.
Branch and MC/DC extraction operate on their own markers and remain active even when ordinary MIR spans are suppressed.
pitfalls: Returning completely empty code mappings when MIR spans are suppressed can make llvm-cov drop the function entirely: the source notes 'llvm-cov seems to ignore functions that don't have any ordinary code spans.'
Do not conflate skipping ordinary MIR spans with skipping branch or MCDC mappings: `extract_branch_pairs` and `extract_mcdc_mappings` are called after the if/else and remain unconditional.
The same signature-only path already existed for async functions; do not duplicate divergent logic for the flag, since the patch makes one branch handle both conditions.
Flag parsing must reject unknown values and update the diagnostics string; the test expects `- `block` | `branch` | `condition` | `mcdc` | `no-mir-spans` was expected`.
Because this is a debugging flag with no semantic coverage guarantee, tests should validate emitted coverage mappings rather than assume normal span refinement behavior.
analysis.testStrategy: Add coverage tests under `tests/coverage/branch/` with `//@ compile-flags: -Zcoverage-options=branch,no-mir-spans` and `//@ llvm-cov-flags: --show-branches=count`, using non-trivial loops (`while a > 0`, `while !(a == 0)`, `while a > 0 && b > 0`, `while a > 0 || b > 0`) plus a `no_merge!()` macro (`for _ in 0..1 {}`) to prevent span merging. Compare both the `.coverage` rendering and the `.cov-map` raw mapping bytes. The expected `.cov-map` must show the signature `Code(Counter(0))` mapping plus branch mappings but no ordinary body code spans, verifying signature retention and continued branch extraction. Also update the invalid-value UI diagnostic expectation for the new option spelling.
evidence: When set, this flag skips the code that normally extracts coverage spans from MIR statements and terminators.
For internal debugging only. If future code changes would make it hard to keep supporting this flag, it should be removed at that time.
